title: Does the Hivemind Effect Show Up in Reasoning Models' Chains of Thought?

original_idea.body:
# Does the Hivemind Effect Show Up in Reasoning Models' Chains of Thought?

**Problem:** The Hivemind study covered standard chat models. Reasoning models produce long CoT, and reasoning patterns transfer teacher-to-student during distillation - suggesting reasoning may be even more homogeneous.

**Direction:** Give open-ended reasoning prompts to 4-6 open reasoning models and non-reasoning baselines, then measure similarity of reasoning steps via embeddings and n-gram overlap. Twist: test whether same-teacher distilled models cluster tighter.

**Why it matters:** If safety-critical deployments rely on reasoning models inheriting one teacher's distribution, blind spots propagate everywhere.

**Relevant context:** Hivemind reasoning-model hint plus distillation-transfer (DeepSeek-R1 distills); models open-weight and small.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible (homogeneous CoT undermines CoT-monitoring diversity) but indirect catastrophic link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Concrete model list, embedding/n-gram similarity on CoT; accessible, no training.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused reasoning-trace homogeneity with a teacher-clustering twist; clear endpoint.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open reasoning models, no lab access; flagged follow-up.

low_compute.reasoning: Long-CoT reasoning models raise inference cost; single GPU but heavier.

novelty.reasoning: Explicit open follow-up; reasoning-CoT homogeneity mostly unstudied.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Reasoning-model homogeneity flagged as open follow-up.
